 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Latest news Social Security benefits can follow you to many parts of the world, but international payment rules depend on where you live.
 Getty Images Social Security Check this list before traveling to these countries: The U.S. government will block your Social Security payments
 Corina González twitter Calum Roche twitter Update: Nov 4th, 2026 03:17 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Each month, the U.S.’s Social Security Administration (SSA) issues Social Security payments to over 70 million people - chiefly retired workers, who account for over three-quarters of all program beneficiaries. The scheme’s claimants also include disabled workers, and the surviving family members of deceased workers.
 Social Security payments can be sent anywhere within the 50 states , as well as the District of Columbia and other U.S. territories, including Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands. Social Security beneficiaries can also receive payments while living in certain countries around the world, although payments are blocked in others.
 The countries where you can’t receive Social Security payments
 The SSA explains that American citizens can continue receiving payments outside the U.S. as long as they remain eligible and are in a country where the agency is permitted to send benefits . The SSA also recommends that beneficiaries always keep their address up to date.
 The U.S. Treasury Department prohibits payments to people residing in Cuba or North Korea . In general, the SSA also cannot send Social Security payments to people in Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan .
 Countries where Social Security payments can be sent
